schema.description: Idempotency-Key header. Required: resending the request with the same key returns the automation the first request created, so a lost response never leaves a second schedule running

post.description: Create an automation that opens a new session with its message every time its schedule fires

description.description: What the automation is for, up to 2048 characters

agent.description: Agent ID string, which follows the agent's latest version, or an agent reference object ({id, version}) that pins one

environment_id.description: Environment ID each run's session uses

initial_events.description: The one user message each run's session starts with

schedule.description: When the automation fires: a cron expression that names a single minute, so it fires at most once per clock hour, read in an IANA time zone name such as America/New_York

repeatArrayField.description: The user message each run starts with, as JSON, YAML, or @file

examples.command: checkfu automations create --name "Morning report" --agent agent_123 --environment-id env_456 --initial-event '{"type":"user.message","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Write the morning report."}]}' --schedule '{"type":"cron","expression":"0 9 * * 1-5","timezone":"America/New_York"}'
examples.description: Run an agent at 09:00 New York time on weekdays

get.description: List automations in creation order, oldest first by default. Archived automations are left out unless include_archived is true. The list catches up shortly after a create or archive, so an automation missing from it does not mean its create failed: to find out, resend the create with its original idempotency key, which returns the automation it created.

post.description: Change any of an automation's fields; the ones left out keep their values. Changes apply to runs that start after the update, and on an active automation a new schedule replaces the next firing. An archived automation can't be updated.

description.description: New description. To clear it, send null for description in a JSON or YAML body on stdin; the --description flag always sends text.

agent.description: Agent ID string, which follows the agent's latest version, or an agent reference object ({id, version}) that pins one

environment_id.description: Environment ID later runs' sessions use

initial_events.description: The one user message later runs' sessions start with

schedule.description: New schedule, with the same rules as on create. A field left out keeps its value, so the expression and the timezone can change separately. On an active automation the next firing moves to it.

repeatArrayField.description: The user message later runs start with, as JSON, YAML, or @file

post.description: Stop an automation's schedule until it is unpaused; it can still be run on request
Resume an automation's schedule from now, without running the occurrences it missed
Archive an automation so it never runs again

schema.description: Optional Idempotency-Key header for safe retries

version.description: The version served, or null when the latest version is served

publication.description: The artifact's public address, or null when it is not published

post.description: Serve an artifact at a public address that anyone who has it can view. Publishing again changes the version served and keeps the address; after an unpublish, the next publish gets a new address. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key is not applied again, so it cannot undo a later unpublish; the same key with another version, or one used to unpublish, answers 409

version.description: Version to serve, or "latest" (the default) to serve each new version as it is added

examples.description: Publish an artifact and serve each new version as it is added

delete.description: Take an artifact's public address down at once; the artifact is kept. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key is not applied again, so it cannot undo a later publish; a key used to publish answers 409
